minutes.headline: TCP committee agreed to keep the extra design scope bare-bones to price a second, rebuild option.
minutes.summary: The TCP Building Design Committee discussed the designer's proposed scope of work for pricing a second option, and agreed to tell the designers it looks right but should be minimal and give a realistic cost. They also covered parking requirements, whether school uses would be state-funded, community feedback, and attendance at the March 25 Finance Committee hearing. January minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned.

votes.outcome: passed 4-0 by roll call (four ayes heard; chair's vote heard as aye)
passed by roll call; all ayes heard

budget_items.topic: Cost figure for the warrant article
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair and Heather are working with the designers on a scope so a number can be provided for the warrant article the select board voted on.

The designers gave separate construction and soft-cost estimates that must be added; the chair asked for one consolidated estimate sheet. Answers on cost-reduction questions (MEP savings after moving from three phases to one) are still pending.
A member said town meeting would likely accept a lower design cost and more reluctantly a higher one.

budget_items.topic: Wraparound road and back parking site work
budget_items.what_was_said: Eliminating the wraparound road and back-side parking was floated as a cost saving; designers were asked what it would save.
Members believe school programs placed in the building would not be funded by the state building program, leaving the town to pay; Brian will follow up.

budget_items.topic: Funding article at Finance Committee hearing
budget_items.what_was_said: The Finance Committee may be split on the committee's funding article, so a committee member should attend the March 25 hearing.

decisions.decision: Committee will tell the designers the proposed scope looks generally right and that they want a rock-bottom, minimal-work estimate, not design development.
Brian will follow up with the superintendent and others on whether school program space would be state-reimbursable.
Members agreed to attend the March 25 Finance Committee public hearing to speak to the funding article; posting is not thought necessary.
Dave Pacios will fill in as chair for the April 21 meeting; April 7 and 21 remain scheduled.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed to tell the designers the proposed scope for a second, rebuild option looks generally right but should be bare-bones, a minimal estimate rather than design development.
Members said school programs placed in the building would likely not be paid for by the state building program; Brian will follow up on whether that space is reimbursable.
Members agreed to attend the March 25 Finance Committee hearing to speak to the funding article, which that committee may be split on.
Eliminating the wraparound road and back-side parking was floated as a saving, and the designers were asked what it would save.
The January 27 minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned; Dave Pacios will chair April 21.

why_it_matters: A cheaper, minimal price for the second option feeds the cost figure in the warrant article, which Town Meeting voters will be asked to approve.
If school uses are not state-reimbursable, the town would carry that part of the cost itself, which falls on the tax bill.
